audit.primary_source_citation: NO PRIMARY SOURCE TESTS THIS CLAIM. The row is anchored on the nearest-to-primary study with the correct experimental architecture: Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, Miao Z, Yin Y, Stickels RR, Chen AY, Hiam-Galvez K, Gutierrez J, Zhang W, Sajjath SM, Valbuena R, Wang S, Daniel B, Ludwig LS, Howitt BE, Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026 Jul 13;44(7):1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233; doi 10.1016/j.ccell.2026.05.006; author manuscript NIHMS2184724 / PMC13309241 (not yet released); bioRxiv preprint doi 10.1101/2025.07.16.665245, PMID 40777278 (CC-BY, full text read); GEO GSE302113 (verified to exist, titled "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer"). HINT VERIFICATION: every element of the hint about this paper checks out (PMID, Cancer Cell 2026, GSE302113, mtscATAC in NSCLC tumour + non-involved lung + blood, myeloid-focused conclusions) EXCEPT the claim that NK were treated "only as part of an aggregate innate category" — see audit_overturns_detail. Largest marker-based source that has ever been offered in support: Nat Immunol 2024 pan-cancer tumour-infiltrating NK reference-mapping atlas, PMID 38956379 / PMC11291284 (427 tumour patients, 136 healthy-tissue donors, 2,176,214 transcriptomes) — which explicitly declines to make the inference.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Published Cancer Cell full text is paywalled (cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(26)00251-5 returned HTTP 403) and the NIHMS author manuscript PMC13309241 is deposited but not yet released in PMC (lit.py methods PMC13309241 -> STATUS=NOT_FOUND). The complete CC-BY bioRxiv preprint (doi 10.1101/2025.07.16.665245, 84 KB incl. full Methods) WAS retrieved and read and is archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X1_dataset_biorxiv_PPR1052262.txt. The preprint and the published paper report the identical cohort and cell count (218,715 cells, 23 samples, 5 NSCLC + 5 ovarian patients), so the methods read are the methods published; I could not verify that no NK-specific analysis was ADDED in revision. All quotes below are from the preprint Methods/Results, not from any abstract.
audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens) for the anchor study. Counter-evidence and adjacent literature audited additionally in mouse (C57BL/6; Ducimetière PNAS 2021, Torcellan Immunity 2024, Horowitz Sci Transl Med 2026) and rhesus macaque (Wu Front Immunol 2022 barcoding).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in freshly dissociated surgical material sampled ONCE at the time of resection (single timepoint; no timecourse, no pre-tumour sample — the organ was never observed before the tumour arose), mtscATAC-seq (joint single-cell ATAC + mitochondrial-DNA heteroplasmy) was run on matched tumour, non-involved lung tissue (NILT, non-adjacent, tumour-free on pathology) and PBMC. Readouts measured were: (a) assignment of cells to mtDNA-variant-defined clones by the Mitotrek framework; (b) cell identity from chromatin-accessibility gene scores at NCR1, GNLY, KLRD1, CD3D, CD8A; (c) per-clone cell-type composition; (d) the fraction of clone-sharing cell pairs for each cell-type pair, within a tissue site and across tissue sites. Measured in 10 patients (5 early-stage NSCLC post-lobectomy with tumour+NILT+blood; 5 ovarian cancer with tumour, 3 with matched blood), 23 samples, 218,715 cells. CRITICAL NEGATIVE: no NK-specific tumour-versus-NILT clone-sharing test was performed; no pre-tumour timepoint, no fate mapping, no photoconversion, no parabiosis, no intravascular labelling, no exogenous barcode exists anywhere in this or any other study for this transition.
audit.n_unit: patients (donors): 5 NSCLC patients with matched tumour + non-involved lung + blood, 5 ovarian cancer patients with tumour (3 with matched blood). 23 samples; 218,715 cells. Cells are NOT the unit of replication. The single NK-informative tumour is n=1 patient (ovarian SU-O-005) and the single NK-informative NSCLC cross-site observation is n=1 patient (SU-L-005). Effective n for anything bearing on this claim = 0.
audit.controls: Within the anchor study: (1) Mitotrek benchmarked against published full-length scRNA-seq of single-colony-derived HSPCs with ground-truth clonal identity, 2 independent donors, 91.3% and 85.3% clone-assignment accuracy at a deliberate sensitivity cost (39.9%/55.1% assignment vs ~80% in the original study); (2) randomised cell-grouping null showing same-clone cells share a cell type more than chance; (3) matched PBMC as the circulating comparator and NILT as the tumour-free same-organ comparator; (4) explicit artefact controls for solid-tissue mtDNA lineage tracing — variants detected in >20% of cells within a sample discarded, cells assigned to multiple clones excluded, correlated variants collapsed — introduced because the authors found high-heteroplasmy variants shared across lineages in solid tissue but not PBMC, attributed to ambient mtDNA uptake and/or horizontal mitochondrial transfer; (5) clone-assignment rate shown to be uniform across cell types and tissue sites (15–26% tissue, 20–32% PBMC), so NK are not differentially dropped. MISSING CONTROL, and it is the decisive one: there is no pre-tumour or tumour-free-timepoint sample of the same organ in the same patient, so "resident before the tumour" is not measurable by this design even in principle. No parabiosis / no CD45.1-CD45.2 chimera / no Hobit or Ncr1-CreERT2 fate map / no Kaede photoconversion of uninvolved organ / no adoptive transfer — none of these are possible in human surgical material.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: De novo acquisition of residency markers by newly recruited circulating NK — i.e. the intratumoural "trNK" was never in the organ before the tumour. Circulating cNK recruited into a tissue acquire a bona fide residency phenotype in situ: Torcellan et al., Immunity 2024 (PMID 38157853, PMC10783803) showed viral and bacterial skin infection recruits cNK that differentiate into Tcf1-hi CD69-hi trNK transcriptionally resembling human tissue CD56bright TCF1-hi NK, Blimp1-dependent. TGF-beta in the TME is sufficient to drive CD49a+CD103+ trNK differentiation from peripheral NK ex vivo (Horowitz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 42090477), and chronic activation alone drives a tissue-resident-LIKE state via KLF2 loss (Blood 2025, PMID 40857665). Under this alternative, CD49a/CD103/CD69/ITGA1/ITGAE on intratumoural NK is a TME-imposed phenotype, not a residency pedigree, and marker identity to organ trNK carries zero lineage information. TWO FURTHER ALTERNATIVES, both with support: (i) TWO INDEPENDENT ORIGINS with no conversion — Ducimetière et al., PNAS 2021 (PMID 34183415) found in mouse liver metastasis that pre-existing liver trILC1 and recruited cNK are non-redundant and functionally partitioned (trILC1 controls metastatic seeding, cNK restrains outgrowth), i.e. the resident and the tumour-active populations are different cells doing different jobs, not one becoming the other; (ii) IN-SITU DIFFERENTIATION FROM IMMATURE PRECURSORS — tumour-infiltrating immature ILCs in colorectal cancer are biased toward ILC1/trNK differentiation (Nat Commun 2026, s41467-026-71085-9), a third origin that also produces trNK-marked intratumoural cells without any pre-existing mature organ trNK. The canonical "pre-existing subset is selected/expanded rather than converted" alternative is therefore not merely unexcluded — it is the better-supported reading, and the recruitment alternative is better supported still.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is substantial. (1) Liu 2026 itself, the anchor: NK cells are DEPLETED in NSCLC tumour relative to NILT ("including enrichment of B and plasma cells and depletion of NK cells in the tumor relative to NILT"); the cell-type-pair clone-sharing analysis puts NK in the group whose pattern "suggest[s] that they originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration" — i.e. recent marrow output, the opposite of long-lived pre-tumour organ residency; and the ONLY NK-specific cross-site clonal result in the organ-matched cohort runs blood->tissue, not organ->tumour: "Among 14 peripheral blood-enriched clones, 10 were dominated by CD8+ T cells and 2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005)... the majority of cells from these clones were detected in PBMCs (66.0%), smaller fractions were present in tumor (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%)". (2) The single tumour with real NK infiltration was OVARIAN (SU-O-005), for which NO matched non-involved ovary was collected — only tumour and blood — so the trNK-before-tumour comparison was structurally impossible there; and its expanded NK clones were "absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response", which is equally compatible with local expansion of recruited cells. (3) Nat Immunol 2024 pan-cancer NK atlas (PMID 38956379): "Compositional differences between normal and tumor tissues suggests some degree of active recruitment, particularly in SKCM where NK cell frequencies starkly increased, albeit expansion from tissue-resident pools cannot be excluded" — the largest existing dataset explicitly refuses the inference. (4) Torcellan Immunity 2024 (PMID 38157853): recruited circulating NK become trNK de novo. (5) Ducimetière PNAS 2021 (PMID 34183415): resident trILC1 and recruited cNK are separate non-redundant populations in liver metastasis. (6) Blood 2025 (PMID 40857665): residency-like phenotype arises from chronic activation via KLF2 deficiency. (7) The field states the test cannot currently be done: "the current lack of experimental tools to block recruitment of circulating NK cells or to specifically target the newly identified resident cells currently precludes testing this possibility."
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY: Horowitz NB, Mohammad IA, Shin JH, ... Sunwoo JB, "CD39+CD49a+CD103+ cytotoxic tissue-resident natural killer cells infiltrate and control solid epithelial tumor growth in mice," Sci Transl Med 2026;18(848):eadw5567 (PMID 42090477). That paper's entire translational proposition — differentiate and expand CD39+CD49a+CD103+ ctrNK ex vivo as an adoptive-cell-therapy platform for solid tumours — rests on the premise that the CD49a+CD103+ NK phenotype found inside tumours is the functionally superior, tissue-adapted state worth reconstructing. Note the irony that cuts against X1: Horowitz make their ctrNK BY TGF-beta-differentiating PERIPHERAL NK ex vivo, which is a demonstration that the phenotype does not require prior organ residency at all. SECOND NAMED DEPENDENCY: within this registry, rows T1 (cNK -> trNK) and T4 (NK -> ILC1 within tumours) are mutually constraining with X1 — if intratumoural CD49a+ "trNK" are recruited cNK converting in situ, X1 is false and the phenomenon is fully absorbed by T1/T4, so X1 cannot be graded independently of them. THIRD: the prognostic literature reading CD49a+ NK accumulation as a pre-existing organ-resident compartment, concretely "Accumulation of Tumor-Infiltrating CD49a+ NK Cells Correlates with Poor Prognosis for Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma," Cancer Immunol Res 2019 (PMID 31311791), whose causal interpretation changes entirely depending on whether those cells were in the liver before the tumour.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: Claude's initial call, "NEVER TRACED," is CONFIRMED and if anything understated. Across 19 distinct searches I found no study in any species that has traced organ-resident trNK present before a tumour into the intratumoural NK compartment — no mtDNA lineage tracing, no mtscATAC, no exogenous barcoding, no mouse fate mapping (Hobit/Ncr1-CreERT2), no parabiosis, no Kaede photoconversion of uninvolved organ, no transplant-genotype study. The claim has never been tested, and no paper I found asserts it on lineage data; where it is asserted at all it is asserted on residency-marker overlap. WHAT THE AUDIT DOES OVERTURN IS THE HINT, not Claude's call. The hint stated that Liu 2026 "reported myeloid findings and treated NK only as part of an aggregate innate category." That is only half right. Liu did fold NK into an aggregate innate group for the headline cell-type clone-sharing statement ("innate immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, DCs, and NK cells, consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing"), but the paper ALSO contains two NK-SPECIFIC analyses the hint does not anticipate: (a) an NK-identity-verified (CD3D-/CD8A-/NCR1+/GNLY+ chromatin) oligoclonal NK expansion in ovarian tumour SU-O-005 whose expanded clones were absent from matched blood, and (b) two blood-enriched NK clones in NSCLC donor SU-L-005 distributed 66.0% PBMC / 25.3% tumour / 8.8% NILT. Neither tests X1: (a) is in the one malignancy with no matched non-involved organ tissue, and (b) runs blood->tissue. The precise finding is therefore sharper than "NK were aggregated": Liu 2026 is the only human dataset ever assembled with the sampling architecture (matched tumour + tumour-free same organ + blood) AND the endogenous clonal marker (somatic mtDNA) needed to test X1, it had NK cells in hand in both compartments, and it did not run the tumour-versus-NILT NK clone-sharing comparison. The test is one analysis away from being answerable on already-public data (GSE302113), and it has not been done. That, not an absence of tools, is the state of the field for the lung; note the residual obstacle that Liu found NK depleted in tumour vs NILT, so the analysis may be underpowered at n=5.
audit.methods_quote: Liu et al. 2026, preprint Results, verbatim: "Consistent with previous reports of adaptive-like, oligoclonal NK cell responses in human cytomegalovirus infection, we observed expanded NK cell clones in NILT and peripheral blood. While NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors, one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005) exhibited substantial NK infiltration. These NK cells lacked chromatin accessibility at CD3D and CD8A loci but showed accessibility at NCR1 and GNLY, confirming their NK identity. Clonal analysis revealed an oligoclonal architecture resembling adaptive lymphocytes. Notably, expanded NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response." AND, on the aggregate innate statement: "innate immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, DCs, and NK cells, consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing, suggesting that they originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration." AND, on the only NSCLC NK cross-site result: "Among 14 peripheral blood-enriched clones, 10 were dominated by CD8+ T cells and 2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005). Although the majority of cells from these clones were detected in PBMCs (66.0%), smaller fractions were present in tumor (25.3%) and NILT (8.8%), indicating their ability to infiltrate tissue." AND, cohort, verbatim Methods/Results: "we applied mtscATAC-seq to profile five patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who had undergone therapeutic lobectomy... For each patient, we collected tumor resections, non-adjacent NILT (not involved by tumor on pathological analysis), and peripheral blood samples." Nat Immunol 2024 pan-cancer NK atlas (PMID 38956379), verbatim: "Compositional differences between normal and tumor tissues suggests some degree of active recruitment, particularly in SKCM where NK cell frequencies starkly increased, albeit expansion from tissue-resident pools cannot be excluded."

audit.notes:
VERDICT: X1 is UNTESTED, not merely weakly supported. There is no primary source; the strongest thing ever offered for it is residency-marker overlap (INF_MARKER) between intratumoural NK and organ trNK, and the largest atlas that could make that argument explicitly declines to.

HINT VERIFICATION, item by item. (a) PMID 42242233, Liu VV et al., Cancer Cell 2026 — EXISTS, verified, 44(7):1509-1521.e4, doi 10.1016/j.ccell.2026.05.006. (b) GSE302113 — EXISTS, verified via NCBI GEO, title matches the paper. (c) "did mtscATAC clonal tracing in NSCLC tumour + non-involved lung + blood" — CORRECT: 5 NSCLC patients post-lobectomy, tumour + non-adjacent NILT + PBMC. (d) "reported myeloid findings" — CORRECT, the paper's conclusions are entirely myeloid (monocyte -> macrophage/DC3 clonal linkage, DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones, peripheral pre-programming). (e) "treated NK only as part of an aggregate innate category" — PARTLY WRONG; see audit_overturns_detail. Two NK-specific analyses exist, neither testing X1.

WHY THE ANCHOR STUDY CANNOT SUPPORT X1 EVEN IN PRINCIPLE, beyond the missing analysis: mtDNA clonal tracing at a single post-tumour timepoint identifies clonal relatedness, not temporal order. A clone containing both a NILT NK and a tumour NK is equally consistent with organ->tumour, tumour->organ, and blood->both. Establishing "resident in the organ BEFORE the tumour" requires either a pre-tumour timepoint (impossible in human resection material) or a residency-locking manipulation (parabiosis, photoconversion, intravascular labelling — all mouse-only). This is why the honest classification is INF_MARKER and why no upgrade is available from the existing human data.

THE TRM ANALOGUE (requested by the hint) DOES NOT RESCUE THE CLAIM — it is the cautionary case. In the far better-studied T-cell field, where somatic TCR rearrangement gives a true clonal barcode that NK entirely lack, the analogous question is still not cleanly answered: TCR-overlap analyses find TRM and exhausted TIL show LIMITED clonal overlap with each other, sharing instead mostly with TEM, and Kaede photoconversion of mouse tumours (Torcellan PNAS 2017, PMC5465915; JEM 2022 TCF-1 trafficking study) shows intratumoural lymphocytes are continuously recruited AND continuously egress to the draining node rather than forming a stable resident pool. So the field with the better tool has not established the structurally identical claim, which makes an NK version of it — asserted with no clonal marker at all — considerably weaker than it is usually presented.

CLOSEST TRUE CLONAL DATA ON TISSUE NK ANYWHERE: Wu C et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, HSPC barcode clonal tracking in rhesus macaque, which found tissue NK have a clonal distribution pattern distinct from blood NK. Correct tool, correct cell type, WRONG SETTING — no tumour. This is the design that would answer X1 if run in a tumour-bearing animal.

CHEAPEST PATH TO ACTUALLY TESTING X1: re-analyse GSE302113 for NK-specific tumour-vs-NILT clone sharing in the 5 NSCLC donors, benchmarked against the CD8 T-cell and myeloid sharing rates the authors already computed. Caveat: NK are depleted in tumour relative to NILT in this cohort and clone-assignment rate is 15-26% in tissue, so the analysis is likely underpowered at n=5 and a null result would not be informative. A properly powered version needs either a tumour type with abundant intratumoural NK plus matched uninvolved organ (Liu's ovarian SU-O-005 had the NK but not the organ tissue), or a mouse autochthonous model with photoconversion or parabiosis performed BEFORE tumour induction.

G-RULE COMPLIANCE: G1 — what_was_measured is stated as species/condition/timepoint/readout/n and never as "showed that A becomes B"; all quotes are from Methods/Results of retrieved full text, never an abstract. G2 — no pseudotime or RNA-velocity result was counted as observation; the CRC ILC-differentiation-bias result is logged as INF_TRAJECTORY. G3 — four searches returned literally zero hits and are recorded as such; NOT FOUND is reported as NOT FOUND, and the one unretrievable item (published Cancer Cell full text, HTTP 403) is declared rather than paraphrased from its abstract. G5 — n is 10 patients, cells explicitly flagged as not the replication unit. G7 — the presence of an OBS_GENETIC-capable technique (mtDNA clonal tracing) in the anchor study was deliberately NOT used to upgrade the claim's class, because that technique was never applied to this transition; evidence_types_all lists only classes actually offered in support of X1. G8 — Claude's "NEVER TRACED" was treated as a hypothesis and actively attacked with 19 searches across four tracing modalities and the TRM analogue field; it survived.
